about.title: About Supercharger Calculator
about.description: The Supercharger Calculator determines boost pressure, power gains, and pulley ratios for supercharged engines. It is useful for supercharger sizing, comparison, and reference checks. Proper supercharger calculations help review boost levels, reduce the chance of excessive pressure, and compare likely output changes alongside reliability considerations.

faq.q: What's the difference between superchargers and turbochargers?
faq.a: Superchargers are belt-driven from the crankshaft and provide immediate boost with no lag, while turbochargers use exhaust gases and have some turbo lag. Superchargers consume engine power (parasitic loss) but offer linear, predictable power delivery. Our supercharger calculator helps compare these system characteristics.

faq.q: How much boost pressure is safe for my engine?
faq.a: Boost limits depend on engine internals, fuel quality, and calibration quality. Stock engines typically stay around 6-8 PSI, while built engines with forged internals may run 15+ PSI with suitable supporting parts and engine management.

faq.q: How do pulley ratios affect boost pressure?
faq.a: Smaller supercharger pulleys or larger crank pulleys increase boost by spinning the supercharger faster relative to engine RPM. The pulley ratio determines supercharger speed multiplication - a 3:1 ratio means the supercharger spins 3 times faster than the crankshaft.

faq.q: What's volumetric efficiency in supercharger calculations?
faq.a: Volumetric efficiency measures how effectively the supercharger fills the cylinders with air. Higher efficiency (85-95% for good superchargers) means more power per PSI of boost, better fuel economy, and less heat generation. Our calculator factors this into power estimates.

faq.q: What are the different types of superchargers?
faq.a: Main types include: Roots (immediate boost, lower efficiency), Centrifugal (higher efficiency, boost increases with RPM), and Screw/Twin-screw (high efficiency, consistent boost). Each type has different characteristics that our calculator accounts for.

faq.q: Do I need an intercooler with my supercharger?
faq.a: Intercoolers are recommended for boost levels above 8-10 PSI to reduce intake air temperature. Cooler air is denser, allowing more aggressive timing and higher compression ratios. This improves power and reduces knock potential.
